Variation: This measure refers to the percentage of the library collection that has been purchased in the last five years. The result is consistent with previous financial years.

Description: Active library borrowers in municipality
Variation: This indicator highlights the percentage of the municipal population that are active library members which tends to vary over time. Active library borrowers over the past three years has been lower due to coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic related impacts.

Description: Cost of library service per population
Variation: This measure captures the direct cost of the library service (per municipal population). The cost of library services has slightly increased compared to the previous year.

Description: Infant enrolments in the MCH service
Variation: Council's Maternal and Child Health Service (MCH) enrols newborn babies once the birth notification has been received and an MCH home visit has been completed. The length of time between notification of birth and MCH home visits can vary for a range of reasons, including prematurity; birth notifications being issued to incorrect Councils; and families moving to new Council area at the time of birth.

Description: Cost of the MCH service
Variation: This measure refers to the cost (per hour of service delivered) by Council's Maternal Child Health (MCH). The cost of the MCH service varies due to a range of factors including: the availability of permanent staff and the need to backfill positions with casual staff due to leave.

Description: Participation in the MCH service
Variation: This measure captures the number of children participating in key age and stage appointments. This figure has increased when compared to the previous financial year, however, participation in the MCH service remains within the expected range.  Factors such as families moving into or out of the municipality can influence this result.

Description: Participation in the MCH service by Aboriginal children
Variation: This measure captures the percentage of Aboriginal children enrolled in the Maternal Child Health (MCH) service. Participation of Aboriginal children in the MCH service varies due to factors such as people's support services being located outside of the Council area and as well as families moving out of the municipality. The identification of Aboriginal children may also not always be recorded as families may not wish to disclose their Aboriginality. There was a slight decrease in participation in MCH services by Aboriginal children during the year, but the result remains within the expected range.

Description: Participation in 4-week Key Age and Stage visit
Variation: This measure considers the percentage of infants enrolled in the Maternal Child Health (MCH) service who participated in the four-week key age and stage visit. The result illustrates there are appointments that were scheduled during the year but not yet attended.

Description: Sealed local road requests
Variation: Road requests are customer requests logged on Council's customer service application Infor Pathway. Requests include line marking, pothole repairs, damaged roads and patching, and road sweeping. The number of sealed road requests is considered to have increased over the reporting period due to more motorists on the road following the easing of impacts associated with the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

Description: Sealed local roads maintained to condition standards
Variation: Council defines the intervention level to be a road condition rating equivalent to 'very poor'. There was only minor variation for this result when compared to the previous year.

Description: Cost of sealed local road reconstruction
Variation: The total project cost associated with the reconstruction of a sealed local road is considered for this measure. The project cost may include but is not limited to traffic control, road base, road surface, kerb, stormwater drain and traffic management device costs.

Description: Cost of sealed local road resealing
Variation: Full costs of sealed local road resealing has significantly increased due to the cost to Council of materials and construction.

Description: Satisfaction with sealed local roads
Variation: Community satisfaction is measured as part of the annual Community Satisfaction Survey. The satisfaction rating of "sealed local roads" is within the expected range. This result can vary for a variety of reasons including, but not limited to: 'local road' not being fully defined in the survey; some respondents taking into account the condition of VicRoads' arterial roads when responding; the term 'condition' not being fully defined; and some respondents taking into account traffic congestion and safety, when responding.

Description: Time taken to decide planning applications
Variation: This measure looks at the median number of days taken between receipt of a planning application and a decision relating to that application. The time taken to make decisions on planning applications remains low at 35 days (on average). This result has been impacted by staff movements during the year and remains well within the target timeframe.

Description: Planning applications decided within required time frames
Variation: In accordance with the Planning and Environment Act 1987, a Council is permitted 60 statutory days to make a determination on a planning application. Decisions on planning applications are within the expected range, but are lower compared to the same time in the previous financial year.  This result has been impacted by staff movements and vacancies during the year.

Description: Cost of statutory planning service
Variation: This measure looks at the direct cost to Council to provide the statutory planning service, per planning application received. The direct cost of the statutory planning service was higher than the previous financial year due to the increased staffing costs due to staff movements and increased workloads.

Description: Council planning decisions upheld at VCAT
Variation: If an applicant disagrees with the decision of Council in relation to a planning application, that person has the opportunity to appeal the decision at the Victorian Civil and Administrative Tribunal (VCAT). This indicator measures the percentage of planning application decisions made by Council, which are subsequently appealed by an applicant and are then subject to a review by VCAT and which were not set aside (i.e. VCAT agreed with the decision of Council). Of the 15 VCAT decisions made in the reporting period, 13 have been upheld by the Tribunal, resulting in a success rate of 95.45% of Council decisions being supported.

Description: Kerbside bin collection requests
Variation: Council provides a comprehensive waste management service that strives to meet best practice standards in terms of kerbside collection.  There was a slight variation on the kerbside bin collection requests compared to the previous financial year.

Description: Kerbside collection bins missed
Variation: This indicator identifies the ratio of bins missed, compared to scheduled bin collections, this includes 120L, 80L, second bins and fortnightly recycling kerbside bin collection. There was a slight decrease in the amount of missed collections, compared to the previous financial year

Description: Cost of kerbside garbage bin collection service
Variation: This measure captures the direct cost of Council providing the kerbside garbage bin collection service (per kerbside garbage bin). The variation in cost of the kerbside garbage collection is due to increases in the landfill levy as well as fuel price increases, but has also decreased as Council's new disposal site is located closer than the previous one which results in reduced disposal costs.

Description: Cost of kerbside recyclables collection service
Variation: This measure looks at the direct cost of Council to provide the kerbside recyclables collection service per kerbside recyclables bin. The cost of kerbside recycling processing has decreased due to Council obtaining a better rate with a new waste processing contract.

Description: Kerbside collection waste diverted from landfill
Variation: This measure refers to the percentage of garbage, recyclables and green organics collected from kerbside bins, that is diverted from landfill. The cost of kerbside recycling processing has slightly increased in the reporting period compared to the previous financial year. The slight increase is attributed to the introduction of Council's Food Organics Garden Organics service on 1 May 2023.

Description: Expenses per property assessment
Variation: This measure looks at the total expenses per property assessment. Over the reporting period, this indicator is increasing marginally, in line with the growth in the municipality and increases in expenditure as a result of price increases for contracts, materials, utilities and enterprise agreement and remains in line with previous years.

Description: Average rate per property assessment
Variation: Over the reporting period, this indicator is increasing marginally, in line with the expected rate increases within the rate cap and the forecast growth within the municipality.

Description: Current assets compared to current liabilities
Variation: Prior period fluctuations were mainly driven by the changes in Accounting Standards, which increased the value of Council's short-term liabilities. The decrease in the current year largely relates to capital grant funding mainly for car park constructions which are recognised as unearned income until spent, resulting in higher current liabilities for 2022/23 compared to previous years.

Description: Unrestricted cash compared to current liabilities
Variation: Higher cash balance in 2022/23 and 2023/24 largely related to borrowings undertaken in May 2022; delays in capital works and maintenance programs due to COVID and supply chain issues over the past couple of years; and additional grant funding for car parks. Future forecasts expect this ratio to then stabilise again from 2024/25 onwards with no additional borrowings anticipated and funds are spent in line with the 10 year financial plan.

Description: Loans and borrowings compared to rates
Variation: This indicator measures total interest-bearing liabilities compared to rate revenue and reflects anticipated increased borrowings undertaken in May 2022 of $10M.  From 2022/23 onwards, with no new borrowings currently projected in the long-term planning, this ratio drops year-on-year.

Description: Loans and borrowings repayments compared to rates
Variation: The higher repayments on loans and borrowings in 2022/23 compared to rates is due to the additional borrowings undertaken in May 2022. As the repayments increase in earlier periods, this percentage is expected to increase across the next three years, before it starts to trend down in 2025/26.

Description: Non-current liabilities compared to own source revenue
Variation: During the 2021/22 period, the non-current liabilities were higher than prior periods, mainly due to large levels of unearned income, which related specifically to grant funding that could not be recognised as income until project milestones are met and the income is recognised in latter periods. This is projected to trend downwards each of the next four years, with less unearned income anticipated.

Description: Asset renewal and upgrade compared to depreciation
Variation: null

Description: Adjusted underlying surplus (or deficit)
Variation: The adjusted underlying result for the 2022-23 financial year has improved slightly from 2021/22 where Council had the one-off impact of the net loss in associates and joint ventures.  However, higher assets write off over 2021/22 and 2022/23 as part of improvement initiatives has had a negative impact on this measure.  The adjusted underlying surplus when these assets write offs are added back are 3.9% and 5.8% respectively. This measure is expected to improve over future years as reviews are completed in asset management.

Description: Rates compared to adjusted underlying revenue
Variation: null

Description: Rates compared to property values
Variation: This ratio has not shifted significantly and is consistent with other prior periods. As well as this, future periods also anticipate similar ratio results.

Description: Expenses per head of municipal population
Variation: This indicator measures Council's total expenditure over the municipal population. The increase in expenditure relates to an increase in employee cost as a result of the new enterprise agreement and increases in material and services costs related to supply shortages and CPI increases. Additionally, current period population size is 1,800 less than at the same time of last year 2021/22.

Description: Infrastructure per head of municipal population
Variation: The value of infrastructure assets has been increasing at a higher level than the population growth as Council's investment in capital works increases post pandemic where works were delayed due to lock downs. Additionally, current period population size is 1,800 less than at the same time of last year 2021/22.

Description: Population density per length of road
Variation: null

Description: Own-source revenue per head of municipal population
Variation: This measures Council’s own sourced revenue. Revenue it generates that on the most part, is not considered statutory, compared to the municipal population. User fees has improved as Council services returned to a post covid normal and facilities opened throughout the year and municipal population decrease has also contributed to the increase of the measure.

Description: Recurrent grants per head of municipal population
Variation: null

Description: Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage
Variation: This measure looks at the relative socio-economic disadvantage of the municipality as derived from the ABS Census of Population and Housing undertaken every five years. Updated census data was made available for this measure in 2022/23.

Description: Percentage of staff turnover
Variation: Even though this measure has decreased compared to last year, it is still high compared to the previous two years during impacts of the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.  The higher turnover is largely driven by an ageing workforce with long term staff retiring or reconsidering their future working options following the pandemic.

Description: Health inspections of aquatic facilities
Variation: Three City of Melbourne aquatic facilities were open during the 2022-23 period, with the Kensington facility closed for redevelopment. All three operational pools have been inspected.

Description: Utilisation of aquatic facilities
Variation: There were 352,178 visits to aquatic centres during 2022-23, an increase of 23 per cent from the previous year. Visitation is based on three facilities as the Kensington facility is closed for redevelopment.

Description: Cost of aquatic facilities
Variation: In 2022-23, the cost per visit to aquatic centres decreased by 36 per cent in comparison to the previous year - from $8.28 to $5.31. This is due to an increase in visitation and revenue which has offset operational expenditure.

Description: Time taken to action animal management requests
Variation: The average time taken to respond to animal management requests is 1.53 days. This is consistent with last year's result and maintains service improvement outcomes achieved in recent years. Understanding how and when our customers want to be communicated with has enabled us to efficiently resolve matters.

Description: Animals reclaimed
Variation: This year 38 per cent of impounded cats and dogs were reclaimed by their original owner. This is a 14 per cent decrease from last year. We impounded an increased proportion of cats during the year and cats are reclaimed at a lower rate than dogs. We are working with neighbouring councils and vet clinics to reduce the number of animals impounded in the City of Melbourne from other council areas.

Description: Animals rehomed
Variation: This year 48 per cent of dogs and cats collected were rehomed. This is a 33 per cent increase on last year and continues an upward trend over the past five years. All avenues are explored to reunite animals with their owner before offering them up for adoption to new owners.

Description: Cost of animal management service per population
Variation: The cost of our service per population has increased by 46.7 per cent this year. This is in part due to a decrease in the population this year. Our service remains cost-effective when compared with other councils.

Description: Animal management prosecutions
Variation: In 2022-23 six animal prosecutions were finalised. Five related to serious dog attacks. The sixth related to an unregistered dog attack causing non-serious injury. As the dog remained unregistered Council initiated a prosecution. All six were successfully prosecuted.

Description: Time taken to action food complaints
Variation: The average time to respond to food complaints is 2.33 days, which is a consistent with previous years.

Description: Food safety assessments
Variation: In 2022-23 we inspected all registered Class 1 and Class 2 food businesses. This result includes the backlog of inspections carried over from the previous year. The backlog was from businesses not operating due to the impacts of COVID-19.

Description: Cost of food safety service
Variation: Food safety costs have increased slightly compared to last year. This is mainly due to employee costs & contract payments.

Description: Critical and major non-compliance outcome notifications
Variation: There were 103 critical and major noncompliance notifications that required follow up in 2022. All were completed.

Description: Council decisions made at meetings closed to the public
Variation: Council made 197 of its 274 decisions at meetings open to the public. Council made 77 confidential decisions in accordance with the requirements of Section 3(1) of the Act. This result is a 34.3 per cent increase from the previous year. These decisions are often to protect commercial or private personal information, such as decisions on grants, subsidiary trading results and contract procurement. Personnel matters, in particular the CEO recruitment process, have contributed to the increase this year. Council committed to make information public in 12 of the confidential decisions, following an operational process.

Description: Satisfaction with community consultation and engagement
Variation: Satisfaction with community consultation and engagement has decreased by 8 per cent. This result remains above the state-wide average of 52 per cent.

Description: Councillor attendance at council meetings
Variation: Councillor attendance at meetings is consistently high. Where Councillors have been unable to attend meetings apologies have been provided.

Description: Cost of elected representation
Variation: The allowances set by the Victorian Government for councillors, lord mayor and deputy lord mayor are higher for the capital city council than other municipalities. 2022-23 has seen a return to pre-COVID activities and associated costs.

Description: Satisfaction with council decisions
Variation: Satisfaction with council decisions has decreased by 9 per cent. This result remains above the state-wide average of 51 per cent.

Description: Physical library collection usage
Variation: Physical library collection usage has increased by 36 per cent since last year - bringing us back to pre COVID-19 levels. We are close to achieving our operational target of 5 loans per physical library collection item.

Description: Recently purchased library collection
Variation: 65% of the library collection is under five years old. This is consistent with previous years.

Description: Active library borrowers in municipality
Variation: The number of active library borrowers is consistent with previous years. Use of our digital collection is higher than pre-pandemic levels, and this has bolstered numbers. There is also a return to physical collection borrowing as seen in indicator LB1 for physical library collection usage.

Description: Cost of library service per population
Variation: Service costs have increased this year due to a significant decrease in the population from 169,860 to 159,813. As a central metropolitan library service we also provide services to visitors from outside our municipal boundaries.

Description: Infant enrolments in the MCH service
Variation: The result demonstrates a high level of engagement with the Maternal and Child Health service.

Description: Cost of the MCH service
Variation: The result of $89.93 is a 9.6 per cent increase from the previous year. This is the result of a change in practise implemented from 1 January 2023. Our appointments have increased to a minimum of 45 minutes to manage the complexity of the work - family violence, mental health and child protection. There has also been an increase in materials and services, and training for professional development.

Description: Participation in the MCH service
Variation: Participation in the Maternal and Child Health Service is voluntary. Regular reminders for missed visits are sent and followed up. Family participation can vary between years. This level of participation suggests a great commitment to MCH services and demonstrates our promotion of health outcomes for children and families.

Description: Participation in the MCH service by Aboriginal children
Variation: The City of Melbourne has a small Aboriginal community. Families can choose to attend Aboriginal Health Services for their Maternal and Child Health appointments. Many use both services depending on the age of the child.

Description: Participation in 4-week Key Age and Stage visit
Variation: The 2022–23 result is consistent with recent years. The Maternal and Child Health Service makes contact with 100 per cent of families following a birth. Some families choose to seek alternative family support services in the early days of parenting to meet their specific and cultural needs. Our service assists these families to connect with other community support services and networks.

Description: Sealed local road requests
Variation: The number of service requests for sealed local roads has increased by 20 per cent this year. This may be due to increased construction activity in the city.

Description: Sealed local roads maintained to condition standards
Variation: The percentage of sealed local roads below the intervention standard and not needing renewal is consistent with previous years.

Description: Cost of sealed local road reconstruction
Variation: The cost of sealed local road reconstruction has increased by 18.5 per cent. This is due to many jobs being completed for a small reconstruction area (<150m2), and a high proportion of work done outside normal business hours to avoid traffic disruption in the central city area.

Description: Cost of sealed local road resealing
Variation: The cost of sealed local road resealing has increased by 31 per cent. This is due to a focus on bus lane resurfacing works, and a high proportion of work done outside normal business hours to avoid traffic disruption in the central city area.

Description: Satisfaction with sealed local roads
Variation: The level of community satisfaction with the condition of sealed local roads is consistent with previous years - despite high levels of traffic and construction activity in the city during this period.

Description: Time taken to decide planning applications
Variation: In 2022-23 the median time taken to decide planning applications was 106 days. This result is consistent with previous years. It reflects the scale and complexity of planning applications in the central city.

Description: Planning applications decided within required time frames
Variation: This year 65.5 per cent of planning applications were decided within the required time frame. This measure has improved consistently over the past two years, from 60 per cent last year and 52 per cent in 2020-21.

Description: Cost of statutory planning service
Variation: The cost per application of the statutory planning service has decreased by 10 per cent from the previous year. Among other factors, improved operational efficiency and increase in number of planning applications while operating at a reduced capacity primarily contributed to the decrease in cost. Beside the reduction, our cost per application is higher than the state average of $2456. As a capital city council we assess a substantial amount of planning applications that are referred by the Minister for Planning and Heritage Victoria. Often, these are large scale complex projects requiring considerable utilisation of resources. While these additional expenses incurred are reflected in the overall cost, the referred planning applications are excluded from this measure, resulting in a comparatively higher value.

Description: Council planning decisions upheld at VCAT
Variation: The number of VCAT outcomes that uphold council's decision has increased by 10 per cent. Only 14 appeals were included in this measure of a total 36 appeals. The low total number of appeals included leads to high year on year variability. 21 appeals, not included in the measure, were resolved with the consent of all parties through a mediated process.

Description: Kerbside bin collection requests
Variation: Kerbside bin collection requests have reduced by 20 per cent this year. The total number of requests is considered low compared to the number of households serviced.

Description: Kerbside collection bins missed
Variation: Missed bin collections have increased by 15 per cent this year. At 3.1 we are well below the state average of 5 bins per 10,000. The total number of missed bin collections is less than 0.004 per cent.

Description: Cost of kerbside garbage bin collection service
Variation: The cost of our garbage collection service has increased by 18 per cent this year. Our cost per property appears higher than other councils as the measure assumes weekly collection of one bin per household. In apartments and commercial developments where bins are shared we provide multiple collections per week and the total number of bins is lower than the number of properties. This results in our cost per property being misrepresented.

Description: Cost of kerbside recyclables collection service
Variation: The cost of our recyclables collection service has increased by 16 per cent this year. This is due to the expansion of our Food and Garden Organics (FOGO) service across an additional 11,000 dwellings. It includes the additional collections and new bin infrastructure. Our cost per property appears higher than other councils as the measure assumes weekly collection of one bin per household. In apartments and commercial developments where bins are shared we provide multiple collections per week and the total number of bins is lower than the number of properties. This results in our cost per property being misrepresented.

Description: Kerbside collection waste diverted from landfill
Variation: We have increased recycling by 100 tonnes compared to last year. This is due to the introduction of Food Organics and Garden Organics (FOGO) services across an additional 11,000 residences in the municipality.

Description: Expenses per property assessment
Variation: Expenses per property assessment is consistent with previous years. The slight reduction is due to an increase in the number of rateable properties in 2022–23.

Description: Average rate per property assessment
Variation: This result shows a 9.6 per cent reduction in the average rate per property assessment. This is due to waste charges being separated from rates for the first time in 2022–23.

Description: Current assets compared to current liabilities
Variation: Current liabilities remained fairly stable, with a slight increase in trade payables at the end of the year. The increase is mainly attributable to an increase in current assets given higher cash holdings at 30 June to deliver on future year’s capital works program. The forecast is for the current ratio to remain stable, and just below 100%, as the cash balances are used utilised in forecast years.

Description: Unrestricted cash compared to current liabilities
Variation: The negative ratio reflects the increase in monetary contributions to public open space received, against the timing of expenditure against the reserve. The forecast is a reduction in the reserve due to public open space acquisitions over the budget and forecast years.

Description: Loans and borrowings compared to rates
Variation: This result reflects the loan balance at 30 June 2023, which is within policy levels and within Treasury Corporation Victoria approved limits.

Description: Loans and borrowings repayments compared to rates
Variation: This result reflects accrued interest and bank fees as at 30 June 2023. This is expected to increase over the budget and forecast years as the loan facility is used for major projects.

Description: Non-current liabilities compared to own source revenue
Variation: The increase in the 2022-23 ratio is solely related to the non-current loan balance as at 30 June 2023. This is expected to increase in the budget and forecast years as the loan facility is used for major projects.

Description: Asset renewal and upgrade compared to depreciation
Variation: This result reflects the increase in capital works expenditure on renewal and upgrade projects over the prior year. This is expected to increase over the budget and forecast years as major projects move further into the building stages.

Description: Adjusted underlying surplus (or deficit)
Variation: The lower negative result reflects an improvement on the prior year. This is due to a significant increase in own source revenue, and only a marginal increase in expenses. We expect the result to improve further and move back into a positive ratio in the forecast years.

Description: Rates compared to adjusted underlying revenue
Variation: This result is consistent with previous years. The slight increase is due to the increase in total rate revenue in 2022-23.

Description: Rates compared to property values
Variation: This result is consistent with previous years. The increase in total rates is in line with movement in property values.

Description: Expenses per head of municipal population
Variation: Expenses per head of population has increased by 7.9 per cent from the previous year. This is due to the decrease in municipal population in 2022-23 over the prior year.

Description: Infrastructure per head of municipal population
Variation: A prior year error was uncovered, where the 2022 result should have been $12,772. The 2023 result reflects an increase in the number of capital works programs in progress and completed during the year. A decrease in the population of 10,047 between 2022 and 2023 has also contributed to the result.

Description: Population density per length of road
Variation: The decrease in municipal population in 2022-23 over the prior year and no change in length of roads has resulted in a decrease in population density per length of road.

Description: Own-source revenue per head of municipal population
Variation: The increase of 16.7 per cent in 2022–23 is mainly due to rate revenue increases relating to one-off impact of rebates provided in 2021-22 and increases associated with the waste levy charge, and a decrease in the 2022–23 municipal population.

Description: Recurrent grants per head of municipal population
Variation: Recurrent grants per head of population have increased by 11 per cent this year and is largely due to a reduction in the population, and a slight increase in recurrent grants.

Description: Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage
Variation: There is no change to this indicator. This information is updated every five years following the Australian Bureau of Statistics Census of Population and Housing. This will next take place in 2026.

Description: Percentage of staff turnover
Variation: The staff turnover rate reduced by 17 per cent this year. This indicates a return to normal levels following an increase in the previous year.

Description: Health inspections of aquatic facilities
Variation: No inspections were carried out in the second half of the year and is scheduled for early next financial year.

Description: Utilisation of aquatic facilities
Variation: Improvements made to the facility and a return to pre-covid access to the facility have seen a significant increase in attendance figures compared to the previous years. Council now has a waiting list for its Learn to Swim program.

Description: Cost of aquatic facilities
Variation:
Expenditure in the 2022/23 financial year is less than the previous year where considerable work was undertaken to improve the facility in 2021/22. 
The improvements to the facility, combined with the relaxation of restrictions imposed as a result of the pandemic, contributed to a significant increase in the number of visits in 2022/23 compared to previous years.

Description: Time taken to action animal management requests
Variation: The average number of days to action animal requests has increased by 6.39% over the last 6 months. This can be attributed to a staff member going on extended leave (9 months) who had the majority of these tasks within their own task list not being actioned. These tasks were subsequently redirected to current staff within the team. Due to this increased workload, tasks are being actioned immediately however there is a delay in staff updating the system as required to accurately reflect the response. It is anticipated that we will again achieve our desired outcome within the next 6 month reporting period.

Description: Animals reclaimed
Variation: A decrease in the reclaiming of animals was due to an increase in surrendered animals (owner relinquishing the care and responsibility of animals to Melton City Council) and a slight increase in cat (excluding feral) impounds. Economic concerns in the community are also playing part in this decrease.

Description: Animals rehomed
Variation: This year’s rehoming rates were proportional to last year. Although faced with multiple separate disease outbreaks of feline panleukopenia virus (parvo) coming from the impound of cats (excluding feral) within the community, our team managed to successfully rehome a significant percentage of animals through adoptions and a dedicated network of rescue organisations.

Description: Cost of animal management service per population
Variation: Results of full year are marginally higher than previous years. An increase in staff wages, costs associated with our facility redevelopment, environmental strain and cost of supplies have together resulted in increase to cost this year.

Description: Animal management prosecutions
Variation: There were 24 matters sent for prosecution with all resulting in prosecutions against the owners of the offending animals.

Description: Time taken to action food complaints
Variation: Council response time has increase marginally over the of pervious years due to an increase in work load and staff shortage.

Description: Food safety assessments
Variation: An increase in the number of Public Health and Wellbeing Act complaints, increased work load and staff shortages has all had a significant impact on the service.

Description: Cost of food safety service
Variation: Council experienced a significant increase in the number of new food premises registered this year compared to the previous year, due to the significant growth in the municipality. This has decreased the cost per premises. Process Improvements and efficiencies have also resulted in lower costs per premises and we were able to absorb the costs.

Description: Critical and major non-compliance outcome notifications
Variation: No notifications received to the end of June 2023.

Description: Council decisions made at meetings closed to the public
Variation: The number of resolutions made by Council at meetings closed to the public in 2022/23 to date is lower than in 2021/22. This is primarily due to a concerted effort by Council to lower the number of resolutions made in meetings closed to the public in an effort to increase transparency and openness.

Description: Satisfaction with community consultation and engagement
Variation: The 2022/23 result is significantly improved in comparison to previous years and indicates the community is generally satisfied with community consultation and engagement.

Description: Councillor attendance at council meetings
Variation: Councillor attendance at meetings in the 2022/23 year was slightly reduced in comparison to the prior year. The return to Council Meetings being conducted in person, currently with no option for hybrid attendance, may have contributed to a reduced attendance rate.

Description: Cost of elected representation
Variation: There was a small increase in the cost of governance for the 2022/23 year. This is at least partially due to the determination made by the Victorian Independent Remuneration Tribunal to increase Councillor allowances, which is reflected in the costing.

Description: Satisfaction with council decisions
Variation: The 2022/23 result is significantly improved in comparison to previous years and indicates the community is generally satisfied with the decisions that Council makes.

Description: Physical library collection usage
Variation: Loans of physical items has increased on this time last year. This demonstrated that the community are returning to visiting our facilities and  re-engaging with borrowing collections.

Description: Recently purchased library collection
Variation: Collection development and collection evaluation is ongoing to ensure that the collection meets the needs of the community.

Description: Active library borrowers in municipality
Variation: Active membership is within the threshold and is relative to the same time last year. This demonstrates that the collections that we provide are meeting the community's needs and the community continue to engage with the library service by accessing resources.

Description: Cost of library service per population
Variation: Expenditure is consistent with the 2021 and 2022 results. Ongoing staff vacancies have impacted overall expenditure and contributed to the marginal decrease compared to those years.

Description: Infant enrolments in the MCH service
Variation: Expenditure is consistent with the 2021 and 2022 results. Ongoing staff vacancies have impacted overall expenditure and contributed to the marginal decrease compared to those years.

Description: Cost of the MCH service
Variation:
The Unit Cost of the service is consistent with previous years with only a small reduction compared to those years. This year has been a challenge for the Maternal and Child Health Service with a significant reduction in nursing staff in line with shortages across the State. 
This reduction has been somewhat offset by: A small increase in service hours being provided with a return to face to face appointments for some age groups as we come out of the pandemic, and Casual staff being employed to meet some demand on Saturdays. The cost of employing casuals is significantly higher than permanent staffing.

Description: Participation in the MCH service
Variation: The decrease in participation is a direct result of increased birth rates combined with a shortage of MCH Nurses, which has resulted in a shift to a prioritised MCH service for infants from birth to 12 months, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children and vulnerable families.

Description: Participation in the MCH service by Aboriginal children
Variation: MCH has implemented new strategies to engage with Melton City's Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander families which has yielded an increase in participation for this group. 221 Aboriginal children attended the MCH service at least once in the year and 276 Aboriginal children enrolled in the MCH service.

Description: Participation in 4-week Key Age and Stage visit
Variation: MCH has worked hard to engage and service the birth to 4 month cohort, however, shortages in nursing staff has impacted capacity.

Description: Sealed local road requests
Variation: The number of sealed local road requests has significantly dropped and is below the materiality threshold due to road resurfacing having been completed on key roads, especially along travel routes to and from new developments.

Description: Sealed local roads maintained to condition standards
Variation: The result for this year is comparable to previous years and continues to be a good result.

Description: Cost of sealed local road reconstruction
Variation: No reconstruction work was undertaken this financial year.

Description: Cost of sealed local road resealing
Variation: There has been a 25% increase in civil costs over the year. Also contributing to the increase in unit costs is a significant increase in the square meterage of resealing compared to previous years.

Description: Satisfaction with sealed local roads
Variation: The increase in community satisfaction is likely resulting from a number of road connections being completed and re-opened or sealed. The satisfaction rating has returned to pre-covid levels.

Description: Time taken to decide planning applications
Variation: The median number of days taken to decide planning applications has increased due to the increased complexity of a number of applications received.

Description: Planning applications decided within required time frames
Variation: There has been a significant decrease in the number of planning applications determined within 60 days which reflects the increased complexity of applications received over the past twelve months.

Description: Cost of statutory planning service
Variation: There has been an increase in the cost of the statutory planning service over the past 12 months due to an increase in the cost of labour within the Statutory Planning and Major Developments Departments and a small reduction in the number of applications received during 2022/23. It is thought the current economic climate has impacted on the number of applications submitted.

Description: Council planning decisions upheld at VCAT
Variation: There was an additional six applications during the year, however they were not decided by VCAT prior to 30 June 2023 and therefore were not included in 2022/23. Of the four applications decided one was found in support of Council's original decision.

Description: Kerbside bin collection requests
Variation:
Since Councils introduction of a flat fee waste charge in 2021/2022,  there has been a continued decrease in the number of changeover bins and reports of damaged garbage bins.  
In 2022/2023,  the number of service option changeovers was halved compared to the previous year. This is primarily due to a reduction in bin options and removal of the price structure on the waste charge (now one flat fee).

Description: Kerbside collection bins missed
Variation:
Council has seen a significant increase in missed services this year. This was due to a number of factors including; turnover of staff, landfill delays (delays in collection times), general municipality growth (new areas & roadworks and the need for re-routing). 
Further to this a change in bin day was completed in the second half of the year, whilst this is required to ensure efficiency in the collection routing, initially the change can result in missed collections whilst drivers and residents adjust to the new schedule.

Description: Cost of kerbside garbage bin collection service
Variation:
Council's kerbside garbage bin service has increased with population growth. 
The annual disposal cost increased by 25% in  2022/23, largely due to the increase in the State Government Landfill Levy. 
Despite the volumes of landfill remaining relatively stable to the previous years, the service has seen a 7%  increase in the number of garbage bins being collected this year.

Description: Cost of kerbside recyclables collection service
Variation:
Council's kerbside recycling service has increased with population growth. 
The annual disposal cost increased by 7% in  2022/23, despite the volumes of recycling remaining relatively stable to the previous years. The service has seen a 7% increase in the number of recycling bins being collected this year.

Description: Kerbside collection waste diverted from landfill
Variation: The kerbside collection landfill diversion rate remains around 43%. Despite processing more due to the growth in properties this is offset by the reduction in recycling stream contamination and uptake of other waste disposal options. In 2022/23, Council conducted a number of waste education related activities with a focus on reducing contamination in the recycling and FOGO streams.

Description: Expenses per property assessment
Variation: The movement in this indicator is largely due to the recruitment of vacant roles from previous year. Council continues to monitor expenditure.

Description: Average rate per property assessment
Variation: Results for this indicator have been consistent over the past few years. Revenue from rates has remained consistent with the increase in the number of rateable properties within the municipality.

Description: Current assets compared to current liabilities
Variation: Favourable movement in this ratio is largely due to inflows of significant developer monetary contributions. Council's liquidity remains strong in dollar terms and forecasted to remain so with substantial cash reserves in place over the medium term.

Description: Unrestricted cash compared to current liabilities
Variation: Movements in actual figures in years 2019-20 and 2020-21 relates to classification of term deposits greater than 90 days as Other Financial Assets. In 2022-23 there was an increase in developer contribution reserves which is reflective of the deterioration in the unrestricted cash ratio. Forecasts assume term deposits are classified as cash. Positive trend is due to projected operating surpluses in future years.

Description: Loans and borrowings compared to rates
Variation: Council continued to repay borrowings as they mature and has had sufficient cash inflows to achieve this.

Description: Loans and borrowings repayments compared to rates
Variation: Council continued to repay borrowings as they mature and has had sufficient cash inflows to achieve this.

Description: Non-current liabilities compared to own source revenue
Variation: Council's Non Current Liabilities continue to remain stable and at manageable levels.

Description: Asset renewal and upgrade compared to depreciation
Variation: Asset renewal expenditure in 2022/23 has reduced. Council assets are largely new and therefore don't require significant renewal expenditure in the short to medium term. Council will have significant growth in assets in the medium to long term and therefore higher depreciation charge.

Description: Adjusted underlying surplus (or deficit)
Variation: The result for this indicator is consistent with the previous year where the economy was coming out of the pandemic. It is largely impacted by the sale of land through Council's Atherstone project. Over the next four years, it is expected this sales revenue will decline as the project is completed.

Description: Rates compared to adjusted underlying revenue
Variation: Council has and will continue to have a high level of growth in rate revenue. Fluctuations in land sales income will impact this indicator.

Description: Rates compared to property values
Variation: This measure has remained stable over recent years. Council is projected to have a high level of growth in rates revenue.

Description: Expenses per head of municipal population
Variation: The movement in this indicator is largely due to the recruitment of vacant roles from previous year. Council continue to manage expenditure prudently despite the high level of growth experienced within the municipality.

Description: Infrastructure per head of municipal population
Variation: Infrastructure constructed within the municipality has and will continue to increase at levels higher than population growth. Increase over the last 4 years is due to the significant amount of contributed assets which is due to a high level of development activity. Recent trend is likely to continue.

Description: Population density per length of road
Variation: Results reflect a significant investment in road infrastructure that has been consistent over the past four years. The population density is reflective of the growth in development within the municipality.

Description: Own-source revenue per head of municipal population
Variation: Indicator is impacted by fluctuations in populations data within the municipality. The 2022-23 result was impacted by significant development contribution income as a result of this development growth.

Description: Recurrent grants per head of municipal population
Variation: The variance is mainly due to 100% receipt of Financial Assistance Grant from Victorian Grants Commission rather than the 75% received in 2021-22 and originally scheduled.

Description: Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage
Variation: Results have been consistent over the past four years. Melton ranks 347 out of 544 local government areas with SEIFA scores across Australia. A low score indicates relatively greater disadvantage in general whilst a high score indicates a relative lack of disadvantage in general.

Description: Percentage of staff turnover
Variation: Staff turnover rate varies from year to year. In the financial year 2022/23 there was an improvement in the ratio as Council implemented an new organisational structure and continued to fill vacant positions.

Description: Health inspections of aquatic facilities
Variation: Councils Environmental Health Officers conducted inspections of 100% of council owned aquatic facilities within the reporting period.

Description: Utilisation of aquatic facilities
Variation: Council visitor attendance is back to pre-pandemic levels. This is a favourable result for Council as we continue to upgrade our facilities, such as Oak Park in 2018 and soon-to-be Fawkner.

Description: Cost of aquatic facilities
Variation: Pandemic-related costs significantly impacted the cost of aquatic facilities in the prior year. All centres are now back to full operation, which has brought down the associated costs of facilities for Council in the current year, with the exception of Fawkner Leisure Centre closure in April for upgrade works.

Description: Time taken to action animal management requests
Variation: Council responded to 1868 animal related requests in 2022-23. Council is committed to delivering a high-quality, risk-based animal management service and this service remains highly responsive. The average time taken for first action on requests was 2.03 days, down from the previous years' 3.72 days and demonstrates Council's commitment to improving animal management service efficiency.

Description: Animals reclaimed
Variation: Of the 503 animals collected in 2022/23, 35% were reclaimed which is up from the 23% for the previous year.  This increase is reflective of the focus Council Officers have placed on the importance of animal registration.  All avenues are explored to reunite animals with their owner however this relies on animals being registered.

Description: Animals rehomed
Variation: All avenues are explored to reunite animals with the owner prior to offering them up for adoption to new owners. Of the 503 animals collected in 2022/23, 51.7% were rehomed to a new owner, down from 61.3% for the previous year.  This reduction in rehoming is balanced with a higher proportion of animals being collected by their current owner.

Description: Cost of animal management service per population
Variation: The increase in this indicator is mainly due to the population decreasing from 184,707 to 174,502 which has impacted the cost per population.

Description: Animal management prosecutions
Variation: There were no animal prosecutions for 2022/23, down from three reported in the previous year.

Description: Time taken to action food complaints
Variation: The average time taken to respond to food related complaints has remained stable at 2.92 days. This maintains Council's average response rate below three calendar days since 2018.

Description: Food safety assessments
Variation: 72% of Class 1 and 2 food premises received a food safety assessment in 2022. Whilst this result is an improvement from 2021, a higher rate of non-compliance prompting more follow-up assessments, difficulties accessing businesses post the Covid-19 pandemic and significant staff changes impacted Council's ability to achieve 100% of first assessments.

Description: Cost of food safety service
Variation: Costs have increased on this indicator due to filling two long-term staff vacancies. Having these positions filled increases the service cost from the pervious year, as well as a minor reduction (2%) in the number of premises registered.

Description: Critical and major non-compliance outcome notifications
Variation: All 277 non-compliances identified through assessments and inspections of food premises have been followed up to ensure compliance with relevant standards has been achieved.

Description: Council decisions made at meetings closed to the public
Variation: Council decisions made at meetings that are closed to the public are when confidentiality needs to be applied to contractual and personal information matters before Council. We aim to have reports made public, with confidential attachments where necessary.

Description: Satisfaction with community consultation and engagement
Variation: The 2023 score has declined from the previous year, however over the long term scores for this indicator have fluctuated.

Description: Councillor attendance at council meetings
Variation: Councillors remain committed to accountable and transparent decision-making, reflecting a consistent attendance record.

Description: Cost of elected representation
Variation: The increase can be mainly attributed to the determination made by the Victorian Independent Remuneration Tribunal that increased Mayor, Deputy Mayor and Councillor allowances .

Description: Satisfaction with council decisions
Variation: The 2023 score has declined from the previous year. The Metropolitan councils as a group, saw a similar average decline.

Description: Physical library collection usage
Variation: This financial year was not impacted by closures or restrictions and saw a significant increase in library users accessing physical collections.

Description: Recently purchased library collection
Variation: Over the last five years we have rejuvenated library collections with newer materials. We also focused on increasing digital collections during the pandemic as they remained accessible despite library closures.

Description: Active library borrowers in municipality
Variation: With libraries back to normal operation, members have been increasing their use of collections. Libraries have also been campaigning to encourage the community to join and/or return to the library.

Description: Cost of library service per population
Variation: Increase mainly due to the additional security required at libraries across the municipality.

Description: Infant enrolments in the MCH service
Variation: This indicator has remained consistent over the past few years.

Description: Cost of the MCH service
Variation: Council has gone back to full delivery post-pandemic and allowing our nurses to see more clients, reducing the service's cost delivery.

Description: Participation in the MCH service
Variation: Council has seen another slight increase in participation in Maternal Child health services this year.

Description: Participation in the MCH service by Aboriginal children
Variation: Another small increase for the financial year with 84 families using the service. Engagement in Maternal Child health programs continues to show the value of the service to families.

Description: Participation in 4-week Key Age and Stage visit
Variation: Council had a number of families transfer out from Merri-bek prior to their four-week appointment.

Description: Sealed local road requests
Variation: The increase is most likely attributed to an increase in wet conditions experienced over the last two years and the gradual ageing of road pavements.

Description: Sealed local roads maintained to condition standards
Variation: Necessary pavement patching works are being undertaken as programmed.

Description: Cost of sealed local road reconstruction
Variation: This increase reflects the current inflation in the CPI and within the construction industry over the last two years.

Description: Cost of sealed local road resealing
Variation: The standard application thickness was increased from 25mm to 30mm this year. The increase in cost also reflects the current inflation in the CPI and within the construction industry over the last two years.

Description: Satisfaction with sealed local roads
Variation: The 2023 score has declined from the previous year. The Metropolitan councils as a group, saw a similar average decline.

Description: Time taken to decide planning applications
Variation: Median days 106 compared to 113 last year during pandemic disruptions, a return to increased performance is now evident for simple applications.

Description: Planning applications decided within required time frames
Variation: Council's performance has improved to be in alignment with metropolitan averages after the pandemic disruptions; the result is within the required timeframes.

Description: Cost of statutory planning service
Variation: This indicator has remained stable for the financial year with a minimal service cost increase.

Description: Council planning decisions upheld at VCAT
Variation: Council results for this indicator are favourable from a now smaller sample with 9 of the 14 applications being held up at VCAT. Many VCAT decisions are now mediated and do not proceed to full hearings.

Description: Kerbside bin collection requests
Variation: There was a slight increase in garbage and recycling collection requests. This was mostly due to missed collections, which comprised 68% of the requests.

Description: Kerbside collection bins missed
Variation: Missed collection requests have increased this year. This was particularly problematic in early 2023 where driver shortages led to kerbside services falling behind schedule.

Description: Cost of kerbside garbage bin collection service
Variation: Increase mainly attributable to increased collection costs and increased waste levy.

Description: Cost of kerbside recyclables collection service
Variation: Increase mainly attributable to increased collection costs and increased processing costs.

Description: Kerbside collection waste diverted from landfill
Variation: Overall the amount of material collected has decreased, with 1953 tonnes less garbage collected; this is despite a marginal increase in properties serviced.

Description: Expenses per property assessment
Variation: Expenditure between 2021-22 and 2022-23 has increased 7% or $13.6 million. This increase is primarily made up of a $4.1 million (14.4%) increase in depreciation costs and a $4.2 million (153%) increase in the loss of disposal of property, infrastructure, plant and equipment. Council also saw an increase in employee benefits, which was as a result of the 0.5% superannuation guarantee and 2.1% enterprise agreement increases. The increase of overall expenditure in proportion to the increase in rateable assessments has contributed to the 7% increase in expenses per property.

Description: Average rate per property assessment
Variation: The result achieved has remained consistent. Council has increased the rate base by the rate cap that is set by the State Government..

Description: Current assets compared to current liabilities
Variation:
The result achieved has remained consistent from 2021-22 to 2022-23. This result reflects Council's strong position to meet current obligations if required.
The reduced forecast in future years is due to the increased capital works program in 2023/24 and the repayment of Local Government Funding Vehicle in 2024/25.

Description: Unrestricted cash compared to current liabilities
Variation:
This indicator has decreased in the current year as Council has invested a greater amount of term deposits over 90 days (which is considered restricted assets) and it shows the impact of capital works carried forward to be completed in 2023-24. The indicator looks at unrestricted cash (cash in the bank and in less than 90 day investments). 
Overall cash levels (both restricted and unrestricted) have remained the same. The split between unrestricted (less than 90 days) and restricted (greater than 90 days) has shifted to achieve best investment outcomes. It is anticipated that in future years the Council will continue to invest for greater than 90 days to achieve the best investment outcomes. Overall cash levels are forecasted to remain consistent with the 2022-23 actuals. 
However, the forecasted shift to increase unrestricted cash is causing the indicator to increase in the first 2-years and then reduce again in the outer years.

Description: Loans and borrowings compared to rates
Variation: Interest bearing loans and borrowings decreased $2 million, whilst rates revenue increased $6.8 million, resulting in the decease reflected between loan and borrowings compared to rates.

Description: Loans and borrowings repayments compared to rates
Variation: In 2021-22 there was a repayment of a $8 million loan. Loan and borrowing repayments decreased substantially in 2022-23, which reflects the decrease for this indicator shown. New borrowings of $8.0 million have been included in the 2023-24 budget, as well as the repayment of an interest only loan in 2025-26 which sees the indicator increase in the outer four years.

Description: Non-current liabilities compared to own source revenue
Variation: This figure is as a result of a minor decrease in non-current liabilities, and a 3.95% increase in rates and charges for 2022-23.

Description: Asset renewal and upgrade compared to depreciation
Variation: The asset renewal and upgrade expenditure increased by $11.5 million in 2022-23. Resulting in the increase shown of 25% which is a great outcome to achieve a low-risk ratio as per the Victorian Auditor-General's Office (VAGO). Council forecasts to maintain a ratio of greater than 100 percent in the forward 4-years. This means that Council is forecasting to maintain the low-risk ratio which is an indicator that ensures that Council is spending enough to maintain its existing assets.

Description: Adjusted underlying surplus (or deficit)
Variation:
The 2022-23 accounting surplus decreased by $7.0 million or 15%. This decrease, paired with an increase in adjusted items such as non-capital recurrent grants and non-monetary asset contributions has resulted in the reduction in the indicator shown.
The main factors for the decrease in the accounting surplus were made up of a $4.1 million (14.4%) increase in depreciation costs and a $4.2 million (153%) increase in the loss of disposal of property, infrastructure, plant and equipment. Council also saw an increase in employee benefits, which was as a result of the 0.5% superannuation guarantee and 2.1% enterprise agreement increases.

Description: Rates compared to adjusted underlying revenue
Variation: The result of this indicator has remained consistent over the last few years.  The small increase year on year is due to supplementary rates issued.

Description: Rates compared to property values
Variation: Property values increased by a 16.7% in 2022-23, whilst rates and charges increased 2.67%. The property value increase in proportion to the rates increase resulted in the variance shown.

Description: Expenses per head of municipal population
Variation: The 13% increase in expenses per head is due to the ABS population figure decreasing from 184,707 in 2021-22 to 174,502 in 2022-23.

Description: Infrastructure per head of municipal population
Variation: Whilst the total value of Council's infrastructure increased in 2022-23, the increase displayed is due to the ABS population figure decreasing from 184,707 in 2021-22 to 174,502 in 2022-23.

Description: Population density per length of road
Variation: While the results have remained in a consistent range, it has decreased this year due to the fall in municipal population.

Description: Own-source revenue per head of municipal population
Variation: The 11.8% increase in own-source revenue per head is due to the ABS population figure decreasing from 184,707 in 2021-22 to 174,502 in 2022-23.

Description: Recurrent grants per head of municipal population
Variation: The result achieved has increased slightly, due to the decrease in Municipal population more than offsetting the decrease in recurrent operating grants.

Description: Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage
Variation: There has been no change to relative socio-economic disadvantage over the past 4 years.

Description: Percentage of staff turnover
Variation: The reporting period has seen a slight decrease in staff turnover from the previous year. A favourable result for Council in comparison to the sector and an overall tight labour market.

Description: Health inspections of aquatic facilities
Variation: All aquatic facilities received an inspection by an authorised officer in 2022-2023 in line with the Public Health and Wellbeing Regulations. In addition to this, the aquatic facilities operator undertakes regular water quality sampling as per their water quality risk management plan.

Description: Utilisation of aquatic facilities
Variation: The increase of utilisation is a result of no closures for the financial year due to COVID-19. This is the first year since 2020 this has occurred.

Description: Cost of aquatic facilities
Variation: The overall cost reduction is a result of flood impacts to the Water Play Park. The floods forced the closure of this facility and reduced operational costs.

Description: Time taken to action animal management requests
Variation: All animal management requests are actioned within 24 hours of being received.

Description: Animals reclaimed
Variation: The proactive work on animal registration and microchipping has had a positive impact on owners being able to reclaim their animals.

Description: Animals rehomed
Variation: The proactive work on animal registration and microchipping has also resulted in a reduction in animals needing to be rehomed.

Description: Cost of animal management service per population
Variation: This is reflective of the direct costs to provide the animal management service.

Description: Animal management prosecutions
Variation: One successful animal management prosecution during 2022/2023.

Description: Time taken to action food complaints
Variation: Timeframes to action food complaints has increased due to staff vacancies and subsequent availability. There has also been additional inspections undertaken in regards to wastewater management, planning referrals and other nuisance matters, which has reduced staff availability for food complaint action.

Description: Food safety assessments
Variation: Staff vacancies have impacted food safety assessment inspections.

Description: Cost of food safety service
Variation: Cost to deliver the service has increased due to price escalation in a number of areas.

Description: Critical and major non-compliance outcome notifications
Variation: Council has prioritised its response to critical and major non-compliance outcome notifications over food safety assessments.

Description: Council decisions made at meetings closed to the public
Variation: The last 12 months included an increase in decisions made containing commercial information. Mildura Rural City Council ensures that all decisions are released to the public as appropriate. Council has recently implemented further training to review decisions made in confidence.

Description: Satisfaction with community consultation and engagement
Variation: Community Conversations have recommenced with the reduced restrictions from COVID-19 and Council continues to embed sound consultation and engagement principles.

Description: Councillor attendance at council meetings
Variation: Councillor attendance at Ordinary and Special Council Meetings remains strong. One Councillor through investigation was suspended from duties which is reflected in these figures.

Description: Cost of elected representation
Variation: This increase includes an increase in the Councillor allowances as determined by the Victorian Independent Remuneration Tribunal. There has also been an increase in attendance at conferences and seminars as facilitated by the reduced COVID-19 restrictions.

Description: Satisfaction with council decisions
Variation: This increase reflects the continued focus for Mildura Rural City Council with emphasis on informed report writing and debates in Council.

Description: Physical library collection usage
Variation: The increase in the use of the physical collection indicates the recovery from the previous two years of COVID-19 restrictions where libraries were closed or had restricted use.

Description: Recently purchased library collection
Variation: Council is committed to the renewal of its library collection. In 2022-2023 the focus was again purchasing of digital material including e-Books and e-Audiobooks.

Description: Active library borrowers in municipality
Variation: A reduction in active library borrowers over the past four years can be attributed to social distancing restrictions and library closures due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

Description: Cost of library service per population
Variation: Council provides a wide range of library services, including five branch libraries, one library agency and a rural outreach library service delivering services to three remote, sparsely populated small townships. The breadth of this service impacts on the cost effectiveness, combined with the Mildura branch opening seven days per week and servicing interstate customers.

Description: Infant enrolments in the MCH service
Variation: Mildura Rural City Council's Maternal and Child Health service continues to receive out-of-state births accessing the service. Some infants that are born or live outside of Victoria, who we do not receive birth notices for, are enrolled in our service.

Description: Cost of the MCH service
Variation: The Maternal and Child Health Service is currently fully staffed for the first time in over 10 years. Reactive maintenance due to storm damage to infrastructure has impacted expenditure.

Description: Participation in the MCH service
Variation: Mildura Rural City Council's Maternal and Child Health Service continues to support timely and flexible delivery of the service.

Description: Participation in the MCH service by Aboriginal children
Variation: An increase of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children accessing Maternal and Child Health Services at Mildura Rural City Council.

Description: Participation in 4-week Key Age and Stage visit
Variation: Mildura Rural City Council's Maternal and Child Health Service has seen 100% of these clients, plus additional families from outside the municipality who choose to use our service.

Description: Sealed local road requests
Variation: There has been a significant decrease in the amount of requests compared to the previous year which was higher due to major storm events that caused road damage across parts of the municipality.

Description: Sealed local roads maintained to condition standards
Variation: Similar trend to previous years that reflects consistent maintenance efforts.

Description: Cost of sealed local road reconstruction
Variation: Increase in costs reflects material price increase and labour cost escalation.

Description: Cost of sealed local road resealing
Variation: More efficiencies in the sealing of large rural road versus urban roads in this reporting period.

Description: Satisfaction with sealed local roads
Variation: The reduction in satisfaction over the past two years can be attributed partly to the major storm and flooding impacts and the associated damage to the road network.

Description: Time taken to decide planning applications
Variation: Staff vacancies in the Statutory Planning department has negatively impacted on Councils ability to process applications within the required timeframe.

Description: Planning applications decided within required time frames
Variation: Staff vacancies in the Statutory Planning department has negatively impacted on Councils ability to make a determination within the required timeframes.

Description: Cost of statutory planning service
Variation: Cost to deliver the Statutory Planning service reflects the direct costs.

Description: Council planning decisions upheld at VCAT
Variation: Council had 10 permit applications determined at VCAT in 2022-2023. Seven of the decisions were upheld (not set aside).

Description: Kerbside bin collection requests
Variation: There has been no significant change to kerbside bin requests for garbage and recycling.

Description: Kerbside collection bins missed
Variation: There has been an increase in missed bins due to new drivers and changes to collection days in areas such as Mildura South.

Description: Cost of kerbside garbage bin collection service
Variation: Increase is in line with normal CPI, Environment Protection Authority levy increases and growth in the number of households.

Description: Cost of kerbside recyclables collection service
Variation: The increase is due to normal annual contract cost increases.

Description: Kerbside collection waste diverted from landfill
Variation: Diversion rate has dropped slightly due to the increase in contamination rates from the 2022 kerbside audit report.

Description: Expenses per property assessment
Variation: This trend has been increasing due to impacts of the cost of the post COVID-19 pandemic and sustained high inflation currently being experienced.

Description: Average rate per property assessment
Variation: While there has been an increase in number of properties and development in Mildura, Council has still been severely impacted by the effects of post COVID-19 and other worldwide events.  Council continues to seek a balance between the demand for services and infrastructure, while also aiding the community's recovery from post Covid and helping cope with the cost of living crisis.  Council also must take into account the community's capacity to pay in accordance with the State Governments rate capping requirements.

Description: Current assets compared to current liabilities
Variation: This result is influenced by the forward payment of the financial assistance grant funding which was increased from 75% last year to 100% forward paid.  Due to supply constraints, cash holdings for carried forward capital works has also increased with several large-scale projects spanning multiple financial years.

Description: Unrestricted cash compared to current liabilities
Variation: Decrease in unrestricted cash held is due to changes in the performance statement model which requires cash held to fund carried forward capital works to be treated as restricted cash. Therefore, this changes Council’s percentages for current and forward financial years.

Description: Loans and borrowings compared to rates
Variation: With the increase in interest rates, Council has sought to offset this by making significant debt reduction over the last couple of financial years.

Description: Loans and borrowings repayments compared to rates
Variation: With the increase in interest rates, Council has sought to offset this by making significant debt reduction over the last couple of financial years. This has led to lower borrowing repayments going forward.

Description: Non-current liabilities compared to own source revenue
Variation: With the increase in interest rates, Council has sought to offset this by making significant debt reduction over the last couple of financial years. This in turn has led to a reduction in this ratio.

Description: Asset renewal and upgrade compared to depreciation
Variation: Mildura Rural City Council aims to have a ratio of around 100% which means we are adequately maintaining our current asset base. This will vary over time and can be influenced by things such as external funding.

Description: Adjusted underlying surplus (or deficit)
Variation: Adjusted surplus is trending down due to impacts of the cost of post COVID-19 pandemic and sustained high inflation currently being experienced.

Description: Rates compared to adjusted underlying revenue
Variation: This indicator varies due to the timing of our Financial Assistance Grant funding and other grant revenue.

Description: Rates compared to property values
Variation: The trend has reduced due to the higher than average increase in property values in recent years. Mildura Rural City Council will tend to have higher rates compared to property values due to the inherent factors of our municipality such as population size, population density, population dispersion and remoteness from a major population centre.

Description: Expenses per head of municipal population
Variation: The trend has increased primarily due to the post COVID-19 pandemic and sustained high inflation currently being experienced.

Description: Infrastructure per head of municipal population
Variation: Increase is in line with capital works expenditure incurred. This included development of several major capital works projects including the Mildura Sporting Precinct, Riverfront Powerhouse Precinct and expenditure on roads.

Description: Population density per length of road
Variation: Mildura Rural City Council's population of 57,156 compared to its extensive road network of 5,179 kilometres across 22,080 square kilometres (largest council in land area in Victoria), results in a low population density per length of road.

Description: Own-source revenue per head of municipal population
Variation: Like many Councils, Mildura Rural City Council is severely dependent on revenue derived from our rating revenue. This year has increased due to a higher than normal recognition of assets.

Description: Recurrent grants per head of municipal population
Variation: This indicator varies due to the timing of our financial assistance grant funding.

Description: Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage
Variation: Mildura Rural City Council is the fifth most disadvantaged local government area according to the 2021 SEIFA index. Only four of the seventy-nine Council's in Victoria are more disadvantaged than Mildura Rural City Council.

Description: Percentage of staff turnover
Variation: Increase in turnover can be attributed to Mildura Rural City Council transitioning out of delivering Aged and Disability home support services.
